title: Contrastive learning
reading: The slide motivates contrastive learning by asking what to do when no label vocabulary exists: the data itself supplies the vocabulary. A large schematic occupies the lower portion, showing two image-encoder branches producing keys and queries, a similarity matrix, and the InfoNCE loss expression.

visuals.description: Two parallel branches: a batch of images fed to a purple 'image encoder' yielding keys k0..kN, and the same images fed to a green 'image encoder' yielding queries q0..qN. A grid of all query-key dot products is shown with the diagonal entries (q0k0, q1k1, q2k2, ..., qNkN) highlighted in blue. Beside it a boxed equation: L = -log exp(qk+/τ) / Σ_i exp(qk_i/τ).
visuals.assertion: Matching query-key pairs (the diagonal) are the positives; the loss maximizes their similarity relative to all other pairs via a temperature-scaled softmax, so supervision comes from the data itself.

concepts.name: Contrastive learning
concepts.why_it_matters: Provides self-supervision without a predefined label vocabulary.

concepts.name: Queries and keys
concepts.why_it_matters: Two encoded views define the positive pair versus in-batch negatives.

concepts.name: InfoNCE loss with temperature τ
concepts.why_it_matters: Formalizes the objective of pulling positives together and pushing negatives apart.

verbatim_spans: What if we don't have vocabulary? From a vocabulary with data itself
